title: Implement Array.prototype.myFlat with Depth & Circular Safety
subtopicTitle: Core Array & Utility Polyfills from Scratch
concept: Recursive Flattening & Sparse Array Hole Stripping
problemStatement: Implement `myFlat(depth = 1)` on `Array.prototype` that recursively flattens subarrays up to `depth` levels and strips array holes, matching `Array.prototype.flat`.
interviewTrap: `flat()` strips holes entirely! E.g. `[1, , [2]].flat()` returns `[1, 2]` without undefined.

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Native array methods must respect sparse arrays (`in` operator check), handle absent `initialValue` in `reduce` (skipping holes to find the first real element), and preserve the caller's prototype chain.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Recursive Flattening & Sparse Array Hole Stripping.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does Array.prototype.flat handle sparse array holes?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Per ECMA-262 §23.1.3.11, `flat()` automatically strips empty slots (holes) in sparse arrays, compacting the resulting array without holes.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests knowledge of modern ES2019 array flattening specification.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How can deep recursive array flattening defend against circular references?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: If an array contains a circular reference to itself (`arr[0] = arr`), naive recursion triggers a call stack overflow. Maintaining a `Set` of visited array references prevents cyclic recursion loops.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests defensive programming in recursive algorithms.

realWorldUseCases.description: Flattening nested comment reply threads or e-commerce taxonomy trees into flat lists for UI rendering.

howToExplain.opening: Array.prototype.flat creates a new array with sub-array elements concatenated up to a specified depth, stripping sparse holes.
keyPoints: Recursively flattens nested arrays up to specified depth limit.
Depth defaults to 1; Infinity flattens completely.
Circular reference detection ensures robustness against recursive cycles.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Flattening nested structures with depth guards is fundamental for processing hierarchical JSON responses.
analogies: Unpacking nested shipping boxes: depth 1 opens the outer box; depth Infinity opens every nested box until only items remain.

commonMistakes.mistake: Decreasing depth after the recursive call.
commonMistakes.why: Depth must decrement as you descend: `recurse(item, depth - 1)`.
commonMistakes.correct: Pass depth - 1 to recursive child calls.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does flatMap differ from map followed by flat?
followUpDeepDive.answer: `flatMap` maps each element using a mapping function and flattens the result by depth 1 in a single combined traversal, which is more memory efficient than creating an intermediate array.
